Jack Burkman, Jacob Wohl Deny Scamming Boosie $600K for Pardon, Boosie Didn't Sign Contract (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
-------
In this VladTV interview, Washington, DC lobbyists Jack Burkman and Jacob Wohl of JM Burkman and Associates respond to Boosie’s accusation that he was scammed out of $600,000 in connection with a potential Donald Trump pardon. The pair deny wrongdoing, saying they were hired as advocates—not “pardon brokers”—and argue pardons are never guaranteed or for sale.

Burkman and Wohl claim Boosie moved forward on a verbal agreement after declining to sign a written contract, and say their work included outreach to congressional offices and pardon-related advocacy tied to his federal gun case. They also address Boosie’s 60 Minutes appearance, disputed text messages mentioning Laura Loomer, Erica Kirk, Mike Johnson, Natalie Harp and Scott Adams, and allegations involving AI-generated screenshots. The conversation covers sentencing timelines, pardon application rules, arbitration, a motion to dismiss, Houston allegations, Trump, Joe Biden, Venezuela/Maduro references and the ongoing public dispute.

Max B sits down with DJ Vlad for a candid VladTV closing segment on accountability, prison survival, and the consequences facing today’s hip-hop generation. Reflecting on his own long sentence, the Harlem rapper addresses young artists caught in serious legal trouble, including Lil Durk, Pooh Shiesty, and the Tupac Shakur murder case involving Keefe D. Max B says anyone facing conviction must mentally prepare for prison, let go of rap-world ego, and understand how dangerous the inside can become.

He also pushes back on judging cases before courtroom facts come out, discusses gang affiliations, New York and New Jersey prison experiences, and takes accountability for his own case involving Pooh Simms and Gina Conway. The interview closes with Max B speaking on family, staying out of trouble, his movement, and Jim Jones saying he has no interest in reconciliation.

recentItems.title: Former Norteño Shot Caller Mario Sanchez on Lil Durk, Keefe D, Prison (Full Interview)
recentItems.description:
Watch the FULL uncensored interview early - become a VladTV YouTube Member now:
https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
Mario Sanchez returns to VladTV to discuss his life story, prison politics, gang culture, major criminal cases, and the lessons he's learned after transforming his life beyond the streets.
Mario begins by discussing his upcoming book, scheduled for release on September 15, which chronicles his upbringing in San Francisco, years behind bars, transition into mortgage banking, financial success, and eventually losing much of what he built. He reflects on why people must outgrow the mentality of their youth if they want to create lasting success.
The conversation dives deep into Mario's experiences as a former Norteño shot caller at New Folsom Prison, where he says he was responsible for 40 to 50 inmates on C Yard during the late 1990s. He explains prison hierarchy, controlling territory, improvised weapons, and the extreme methods inmates use to move contraband while avoiding detection.
Mario and Vlad also discuss several high-profile criminal cases, including the Lil Durk murder-for-hire trial and Keefe D's case. Drawing from his own experiences, Mario explains how informants and cooperating witnesses can dismantle entire organizations and discusses large RICO prosecutions involving Norteño street gangs.
The conversation expands into the psychology behind street violence, with Mario arguing that many life-changing crimes are committed by young men who lack maturity or are under the influence of drugs. He also shares his perspective on the death penalty in extreme cases and the importance of strong evidence before imposing irreversible punishment.
Finally, Mario addresses the longstanding conflict between the Mexican Mafia and Nuestra Familia, arguing that Mexican American communities would benefit more from focusing on larger issues affecting their communities rather than continuing generations of internal gang warfare.

In this VladTV interview, former U.S. special operations veterans Nicholas Irving and Robert O’Neill weigh in on the Israel-Hamas war, civilian casualties, AI targeting, and the limits of judging combat decisions from afar. Irving says Israel “could do a better job” protecting civilians, while cautioning that outsiders don’t see the realities on the ground. O’Neill adds perspective on battlefield pressure, media narratives, and the split-second choices that can lead to death, prison, or capture.

The conversation turns to the wider Middle East conflict, Hamas’ refusal to recognize Israel, and whether negotiation is possible. Both guests separate criticism of Israel from criticism of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, with O’Neill referencing unrest before October 7 and Netanyahu’s legal vulnerability if he leaves office. Irving agrees Netanyahu is “the issue,” prompting dark jokes about Mossad and fears of being assassinated for speaking openly.

DJ Vlad and Trap Lore Ross analyze the next phase of Lil Durk’s federal legal battle, with Vlad insisting an October trial date is unlikely as new filings, bond motions, and behind-the-scenes legal strategy could push the case back. Ross weighs whether Durk’s defense might benefit from moving quickly before prosecutors expand the case into a broader RICO involving OTF, alleged racketeering, and additional co-conspirators.

The conversation also revisits the Beverly Hills shooting that killed Lul Pab, Quando Rondo’s trauma, Lul Tim’s role, and the recent convictions of DD and David Lindsay for stalking resulting in death. Vlad and Ross discuss why a potential civil lawsuit from Lul Pab’s mother could still create major financial consequences for Durk, comparing the lower burden of proof to the O.J. Simpson civil case. Ross also reflects on covering the federal trial firsthand for VladTV despite harassment and security concerns.
